traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.4, 0.37, 0.33], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.twig_colour.note: Wikipedia, Asimina triloba (read 2026-10-19): branchlets "Light brown, tinged with red, marked by shallow grooves". The colour is our reading of the words; iNaturalist photos read grey-brown, Lab L about 45 (imagekit pawpaw trial, 2026-10-18), where the bark's colour drew the twigs silver-grey (L about 82).

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Asimina triloba (read 2026-10-18): "In autumn, the leaves are a rusty yellow". Colour ours.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's pawpaw review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): "grows from 20 to 40 feet (6-12 m) tall". FNA vol. 3 gives shrubs or trees 1.5-11(-14) m.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 15-30 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): petiole 5-10 mm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade oblong-obovate to oblanceolate, thin, narrowly wedge-shaped at the base.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's pawpaw review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): "a native, deciduous, large shrub or small tree".

traits.clonal.note: FEIS's pawpaw review (Sullivan 1993, read 2026-10-16): it grows clonally from root suckers, forming thickets or small colonies.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers 2-4(-5) cm across.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers maroon (Dendrology p. 84: dark purplish brown). The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.inflorescence.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 84, Asimina triloba: flowers solitary in the axils, nodding on a stalk 1.5-2 cm.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers from the previous year's shoots, before or as the new leaves come out, on a nodding stalk 1.5-2 cm.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): pistils 3-7(-12).

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): berries yellow-green, 5-15 cm.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): berries 5-15 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Asimina triloba (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): berries yellow-green. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 84, Asimina triloba: flowers April-May, before or with the leaves (FEIS: February to May by latitude).

traits.fruiting_months.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 84, Asimina triloba: fruit ripe September-October (FEIS: July to September).

generator.params.note: Red alder's crown values, changed by hand for a small understory tree: one slender trunk (FEIS: usually single), spreading-ascending branches (FNA), a narrower crown and shorter shoots, flowers drawn 3 cm across (FNA: 2-4 cm), path_half fitted so it reaches its height. Not fitted to measurements. Short-shoot leaves take the decurrent-tree rule's size (0.88 of leaf_size): the hand-set card of 0.337 m, from when leaf_size was 1.5 times the flora's blade, drew every leaf 33 cm long and its petiole 1 cm, past FNA's 15-30 cm and 5-10 mm. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius.

allometry.note: 7 m at 25 years in the open, within FEIS's 6-12 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FNA vol. 3 and FEIS: thin, shallowly furrowed grey-brown bark; large, thin, drooping obovate leaves. The leaf card's petiole is 0.03 of its length, the flora's petiole against blade and petiole together.

traits.life_span.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2655435), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2655435), as no source read gives it.

traits.sexual_system.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2655435), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruitlets.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Asimina (read 2026-10-17): fleshy berries; each flower's three to seven pistils ripen one to several berries together, in clusters of one to four, rarely more (Pomper and Layne 2005, as a review cites them).
